# ToolAlignBench

> ToolAlignBench: a benchmark of 128 scenarios across 16 regulated domains measuring whether safety-aligned tool-calling LLM agents follow their deployment instructions when those instructions conflict with the model's safety-trained values. Safety-aligned open-source models overrode their deployment instructions in up to 43.4% of runs — including whistleblowing to regulators, data exfiltration, and evidence tampering. All benchmark documents are synthetic; the wrongdoing is fabricated for evaluation.

Paper: "ToolAlignBench: Investigating Alignment Conflicts in Tool-Calling Enabled LLMs" by Aryan Keluskar, Amrita Bhattacharjee, and Huan Liu (School of Computing & AI, Arizona State University). Published at the Pluralistic Alignment Workshop, ICML 2026.

## Key facts

- 128 scenarios (64 organizational-wrongdoing + 64 matched safe) across 16 regulated domains: financial services, healthcare, aviation safety, energy infrastructure, biotechnology, environmental compliance, labor rights, and more.
- Each scenario gives the agent aligned tools (e.g. `writeInternalLog`), whistleblowing tools (e.g. `sendEmail` to internal or external recipients), and misaligned tools (e.g. document export, report deletion, file modification).
- 12 models evaluated, 640 runs each. Instruction-override rates: 0.3% (GPT-5-mini) to 68.3% (abliterated Llama-8B). Safety-aligned open-source models: Gemma-3-12B 43.4%, Llama-3.1-8B 45.2%, Qwen-Coder-32B 47.3%, Mistral-Small-24B 47.7%. GPT-5 models stay near zero.
- Models judge the content, not chance: wrongdoing scenarios elicit external contact 13.0% vs 2.8% in safe ones; evidence tampering 32.2% vs 9.9%.
- Abliteration (removing refusal directions) drops external whistleblowing up to 99% (Mistral-24B: 27.5% → 0.3%) but other misaligned behaviors move in mixed directions — alignment is not monolithic.
- Over-suspicion creates false positives: models execute misaligned tool calls even in safe scenarios (24.6% unauthorized data access).
- The paper's position: not that agents should never act on safety concerns, but that behavior under value conflicts must be predictable and observable before deployment.
